method: FIXTURE, not real data. Waterline does not simulate rainfall, drainage or how water arrives: each slider depth is a scenario, tied to real elevations by setting the outside water surface to the estimated floor elevation plus that depth. The floor is the USGS ground elevation at the building (NAVD 88) plus an assumed slab allowance, and FEMA's 1% annual-chance flood level (NAVD 88) is placed on the same scale for reference.

datum.name: NAVD 88
datum.usgs: The USGS Elevation Point Query Service returns elevations interpolated from 3DEP; 3DEP elevations over the contiguous US are referenced to NAVD 88. The service's response itself states no datum.
datum.fema: FEMA's NFHL records V_DATUM NAVD88 and LEN_UNIT Feet on every line used.
sources: USGS FAQ 'How accurate are elevations generated by the Elevation Point Query Service in The National Map?' (updated 2025-07-18): EPQS returns elevations interpolated from the 3DEP dynamic elevation service; overall RMSE 0.53 m. https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/how-accurate-are-elevations-generated-elevation-point-query-service-national-map

USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second DEM metadata (catalog.data.gov, publisher U.S. Geological Survey, updated 2025-02-14): over the contiguous United States elevations are referenced to the North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD88). https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/1-3rd-arc-second-digital-elevation-models-dems-usgs-national-map-3dep-downloadable-data-co

FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer, https://hazards.fema.gov/arcgis/rest/services/public/NFHL/MapServer: layer 14 Cross-Sections (WSEL_REG, V_DATUM, LEN_UNIT), layer 16 Base Flood Elevations (ELEV, V_DATUM, LEN_UNIT)
datum.note: Both are NAVD 88 in feet, so they are compared directly with no conversion. USGS feet are international feet; the difference from survey feet is under 0.001 ft at these elevations.

ground.sentence: Ground next to the walls runs from 52.0 to 52.8 ft NAVD 88; lowest on the south side, highest on the north side. Within 40 m it runs from 51.0 to 54.5 ft.

first_door.sentence: The ground is lowest in front of the dock door on the east side, 3.5 ft lower than at the next door (drive-in, north), so water collects there first. A dock door opens at floor height, so water enters through it only once it reaches the floor.

floor.basis: the ground in front of the 1 door that sets the floor, plus 0-0.5 ft (G-SLAB-GRADE: Drive-in doors at grade: the slab meets the ground at the drive-in door, within half a foot.) The range includes the USGS ground accuracy (±1.74 ft, 1 RMSE).
floor.chosen_because: drive-in doors at grade: 1 mapped from the aerial images, CoStar records 2

fema_1pct.basis: the two nearest cross-sections on FIXTURE BAYOU (40 m, 120 m away), weighted by inverse distance
fema_1pct.sentence: FEMA's 1% flood level at this building (53.4 ft NAVD 88) is about 1.0 ft above this floor (range -1.2 to +3.2 ft): about 1.0 ft of water inside. Within the uncertainty it could fall either side of the floor.

reference_levels.label: FEMA 1% annual-chance flood level
reference_levels.source: FEMA NFHL: the two nearest cross-sections on FIXTURE BAYOU (40 m, 120 m away), weighted by inverse distance
reference_levels.sentence: FEMA's 1% flood level at this building (53.4 ft NAVD 88) is about 1.0 ft above this floor (range -1.2 to +3.2 ft): about 1.0 ft of water inside. Within the uncertainty it could fall either side of the floor.

reference_levels.label: Ground at the lowest door
reference_levels.source: USGS EPQS (3DEP), sampled 2 m outside the door
reference_levels.sentence: Ground at the lowest door is 48.6 ft NAVD 88, 3.8 ft below this floor: water there is about 3.8 ft deep before any reaches the floor.

assumptions.text: Ground elevation from USGS EPQS (3DEP, NAVD 88, feet): 12 points 3 m outside the walls, 8 on a grid up to 40 m around, and one 2 m in front of each mapped door. Vertical accuracy: RMSE 0.53 m (1.74 ft), the service's stated overall figure.
assumptions.source: USGS FAQ 'How accurate are elevations generated by the Elevation Point Query Service in The National Map?' (updated 2025-07-18): EPQS returns elevations interpolated from the 3DEP dynamic elevation service; overall RMSE 0.53 m. https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/how-accurate-are-elevations-generated-elevation-point-query-service-national-map

assumptions.text: Drive-in doors at grade: the slab meets the ground at the drive-in door, within half a foot. Chosen because: drive-in doors at grade: 1 mapped from the aerial images, CoStar records 2.

FEMA 1% annual-chance water surface from NFHL cross-sections (WSEL_REG) nearest the building, range between the two nearest on the nearest flooding source, nearest Base Flood Elevation line as a check.
assumptions.source: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer, https://hazards.fema.gov/arcgis/rest/services/public/NFHL/MapServer: layer 14 Cross-Sections (WSEL_REG, V_DATUM, LEN_UNIT), layer 16 Base Flood Elevations (ELEV, V_DATUM, LEN_UNIT)

assumptions.text: Water inside rises to the outside level: the outside water surface for a slider step is the floor elevation plus the depth. Waterline does not model rainfall, drainage or flow.
